scenario_stem: A bank must keep customer account data in its own data center for regulatory reasons, but it wants to run its public marketing site and seasonal analytics workloads on a public cloud provider, with the two environments connected. Which deployment model is this?

explanation.correct: A hybrid cloud combines on-premises or private infrastructure with public cloud services and connects them, so each workload can run where it fits best.

distractors.A: A private cloud runs only on infrastructure dedicated to one organisation; it doesn't include the public cloud portion.
distractors.B: A purely public cloud deployment would move the account data out of the bank's own data center, which it can't do.
distractors.D: A community cloud is shared by several organisations with common requirements, such as a group of government agencies.

scenario_stem: An application must keep running if a single data center loses power, and its servers need very low latency between each other. Where should the company deploy them?

options.A: On one large instance in a single availability zone
options.B: Across multiple availability zones in one region
options.D: On edge locations of a content delivery network

explanation.correct: Availability zones are physically separate data centers within one region, connected by fast, low-latency links. Spreading servers across them survives a single data center failure without the latency of long distances.

distractors.A: A single instance in one zone is a single point of failure; if that data center goes down, so does the application.
distractors.C: Multi-region deployments protect against a whole region failing, but the distance adds latency that this application can't tolerate.
distractors.D: CDN edge locations cache content close to users; they don't host the application's servers.

scenario_stem: A team needs to resize images whenever a user uploads one. Uploads are unpredictable, sometimes none for hours, and the team wants to pay nothing while nothing is happening. Which approach fits best?

options.A: A virtual machine that polls the storage bucket every minute
options.B: A serverless function triggered by the upload event
options.C: A container cluster sized for peak load
options.D: A reserved instance running an image server

explanation.correct: A serverless function runs only when an upload event triggers it, scales automatically with bursts, and is billed per execution, so idle periods cost nothing.

distractors.A: A polling virtual machine is billed for every hour it runs, even when there is nothing to process.
distractors.C: A cluster sized for peak load pays for that capacity all the time, including the hours with no uploads.
distractors.D: A reserved instance is a commitment to run continuously, the opposite of paying only when there is work.

scenario_stem: A three-tier application has a public load balancer, application servers and a database. The security team wants the database to be unreachable from the internet. Which design achieves this?

options.A: Put the database in a public subnet with a strong password
options.B: Put the database in a private subnet and allow inbound traffic only from the application servers' security group
options.C: Give the database a public IP address but change its default port
options.D: Put the database behind the same public load balancer as the web tier

explanation.correct: A private subnet has no route from the internet, and a firewall rule that admits only the application tier limits who can connect even from inside the network. Together they keep the database off the internet.

distractors.A: A strong password helps, but a database in a public subnet can still be reached and attacked from the internet.
distractors.C: Changing the port is obscurity, not protection; port scans find the service quickly.
distractors.D: Placing the database behind a public load balancer would expose it to the internet, the opposite of the goal.

scenario_stem: A production storage bucket was deleted overnight. The operations manager needs to find out which identity deleted it, when, and from which IP address. Where should they look?

options.B: The provider's audit log of management API calls

explanation.correct: Cloud providers record management (control-plane) API calls in an audit log, including the caller's identity, the time, the action and the source IP address.

distractors.A: Application logs record what the application does; a bucket deleted through the console or API wouldn't appear there.
distractors.C: Utilisation metrics measure performance, not who performed an action.
distractors.D: Billing reports show costs per resource and usually lag by hours or days; they don't identify who made a change.

scenario_stem: A team's staging and production environments keep drifting apart because engineers make manual changes in the provider's web console. What practice best prevents this?

options.A: Document every manual change in a shared spreadsheet
options.B: Define the infrastructure as code, keep it in version control and apply changes through a pipeline
options.C: Restrict console access to one senior engineer
options.D: Take a screenshot of each environment's settings every week

explanation.correct: Infrastructure as code describes each environment in reviewable, versioned files. Applying the same templates to staging and production keeps them consistent, and drift shows up as a difference from the code.

distractors.A: A spreadsheet records changes after the fact but doesn't stop the environments diverging, and it is easy to forget to update.
distractors.C: Limiting access to one person reduces who can make changes but still leaves them manual and unrepeatable.
distractors.D: Screenshots can show that drift happened but do nothing to prevent it or to rebuild an environment.

scenario_stem: Users occasionally report that a checkout page is slow, but by the time the team checks, everything looks fine. The team wants to be notified as soon as performance degrades. What should they set up?

options.A: An alarm on the 95th-percentile response-time metric that notifies the on-call engineer
options.B: A weekly report of average CPU usage
options.C: Larger instances for the checkout service
options.D: Manual spot checks of the page every morning

explanation.correct: An alarm on a latency metric such as the 95th percentile fires when slow requests appear, so the team learns about the problem while it is happening.

distractors.B: A weekly CPU average is too infrequent to catch short slowdowns and may not reflect response time at all.
distractors.C: Bigger instances might hide the symptom, but they don't tell the team when or why the slowdown happens.
distractors.D: Spot checks only sample one moment a day and would miss most intermittent problems.

scenario_stem: A business states that, after an outage, it can afford to lose at most 15 minutes of order data. Which recovery metric does this requirement define?

explanation.correct: The RPO is the maximum acceptable amount of data loss, measured as time before the failure. A 15-minute RPO means backups or replication must capture changes at least every 15 minutes.

distractors.A: The RTO is how long it may take to restore service after an outage, not how much data may be lost.
distractors.C: MTBF measures how often a system fails on average; it doesn't set a limit on data loss.
distractors.D: An SLA uptime percentage promises availability over a period and says nothing about how much data can be lost.
